announced.quote: By June 15, the experimenters were confident in their results, and Steve Herb announced the discovery at a June 30 seminar in the Fermilab Auditorium.

date.note: First public announcement, a seminar at Fermilab; the Fermilab July 1 page says Herb announced the discovery "at a June 30 seminar in the Fermilab Auditorium".
date.quote: 6/30/77 Steve Herb announced the Upsilon (9.5) discovery in a seminar at Fermilab

key_value.note: Mass of the enhancement as stated in the abstract.
key_value.quote: A strong enhancement is observed at 9.5 GeV mass in a sample of 9000 dimuon events with a mass mμ+μ−>5 GeV.

name: Observation of a Dimuon Resonance at 9.5 GeV in 400-GeV Proton-Nucleus Collisions
notes: The paper title says "Observation"; the discovery label comes from Fermilab ("Discovery of the bottom quark"), so the type follows the title (A16).
The text of Lederman's lecture ("a paper was sent off in August of 1977") disagrees with the Fermilab and APS dates; the APS publication date is used.

published.note: Publication date; Fermilab says the paper was submitted on 1 July 1977.

summary.plain: The E288 team at Fermilab reported a clear bump in pairs of muons at 9.5 GeV from 400 GeV proton collisions. It was a new particle, the upsilon, later understood as a bottom quark bound to its antiquark.
summary.technical: A strong enhancement at 9.5 GeV in a sample of 9000 dimuon events with m(μ⁺μ⁻) > 5 GeV from 400-GeV protons on nuclei; later understood as the bound state of a bottom quark and its antiquark.

title: Observation of a Dimuon Resonance at 9.5 GeV in 400-GeV Proton-Nucleus Collisions
why_it_matters: Fermilab History and Archives says the upsilon "was later understood to be the bound state of the bottom quark and its antiquark".
